item.title: February freight shipments and expenditures see annual gains in February, reports Cass Freight Index
item.description: The February shipments reading, at 0.978, fell 7.2% annually, in line with January’s 7.1% annual decline, which indicated a new cycle low in January. February expenditures, at 3.143, were up 2.1% annually, an improvement over January’s 0.6% annual gain, and rose 5.1% sequentially

item.title: What to expect at MODEX 2026
item.description: Get ready for Modex 2026 with Modern

item.title: Intermodal volumes bounce back in February, states IANA
item.description: Total February volume, at 1,462,429 units, increased 2.7% annually, following a 5.9% annual decline in January.

item.title: National diesel average climbs up for 12th consecutive week, reports EIA
item.description: For the week of March 23, EIA data showed that the national average price per gallon, at $5.375, was up for the 12th consecutive week, rising $1.808 annually and up 30.4 cents compared to the week of May 16, which came in at $5.071.

item.title: Prologis and GIC roll out a $1.6 bilion U.S. logistics venture
item.description: The joint venture focuses on build-to-suit facilities tied to e-commerce demand.

item.title: U.S. rail carload and intermodal volumes see annual gains, for week ending March 21, reports AAR
item.description: Rail carloads, at 227,252, rose 1.2% annually, and intermodal containers and trailers, at 274,669, units, were up 1.2% annually.

item.title: ‘Physical AI’ is shaping warehouse operations beyond traditional visibility
item.description: As supply chains push past traditional visibility tools, a new class of physical AI is digitizing real-world warehouse activity.

item.title: Hiring slows down as tariffs and costs weigh on manufacturers
item.description: U.S. manufacturing is under pressure, with job losses mounting as tariffs, rising costs, and ongoing uncertainty continue to weigh on hiring and investment.

item.title: NextGen conference revamps awards for 2026, opens submissions
item.description: Updated categories, a new partnership-focused award, and a May 15 deadline set the stage for recognizing real-world supply chain execution.

item.title: Modex keynote panel will preview 2026 MHI annual industry report findings
item.description: The session, Rewiring the Future: A Supply Chain Playbook for Innovation, previews the report’s findings and puts them into real-world context.

item.title: UPS pulls driver buyout program after pushback from the Teamsters
item.description: The International Brotherhood of Teamsters said UPS informed the union on March 24 that it would withdraw the program across the region, which covers 13 states from Nebraska to Ohio. The union said the move affects more than a dozen states and could make it harder for UPS to continue similar buyout offers elsewhere under the National Master Agreement.

item.title: National diesel average increases for 13th consecutive week, reports EIA
item.description: EIA data showed that the national average price per gallon, at $5.401, was up for the 13th consecutive week, rising $1.809 annually and up 2.6 cents compared to the week of March 23.

item.title: Amazon brings on 1,500 FedEx sites to its returns network
item.description: The move expands Amazon’s network to more than 10,000 drop-off locations.

item.title: Diesel surge tightens truckload capacity, pushes spot rates higher
item.description: Total load posts rose slightly to 3.99 million, for the week of March 22-28, suggesting demand remained steady as available capacity contracted.

item.title: Amazon Freight increases dry van trailer count to 80,000
item.description: The company said this marks an expansion from its previous trailer count, of 70,000 less than a year ago.
